title: Migrations apply atomically; a crash mid-migration leaves the previous version intact
asA: operator whose deploy must never leave the store in a half-migrated state
iWant: each migration to run inside a single transaction with the version bookkeeping row committed alongside its statements
soThat: an abrupt failure during migration N leaves the store on version N-1, not on some undefined mixture

acceptanceCriteria.description: The migration runner applies pending migrations in ascending version order; for each migration, the version bookkeeping row and the migration's statements are committed in one transaction.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a store opened against a file older than the build's max known version with pending migrations v_k+1 through v_n
acceptanceCriteria.then: the bookkeeping table holds one row for each of v_k+1 through v_n in ascending order, and every domain table shape reflects the union of statements from those migrations

acceptanceCriteria.description: A migration whose statements or version bookkeeping row fails is rolled back; the on-disk highest bookkeeping row after the failed run is the last successfully committed version.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a store at version v_k and a pending migration v_k+1 whose statements will throw at execution time
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration runner attempts v_k+1 and its transaction fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the bookkeeping table's highest row remains v_k, no partial DDL from v_k+1 is present, and the migration runner throws an error naming version v_k+1 and the failing description

acceptanceCriteria.description: The migration runner does not attempt migrations later than the first failing one; a failure at v_k+1 leaves v_k+2 and beyond unattempted.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a store at version v_k and pending migrations v_k+1 (failing) and v_k+2 (would succeed)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the migration runner runs and fails on v_k+1
acceptanceCriteria.then: no domain-table statements from v_k+2 have been executed and the bookkeeping table holds no row for v_k+2
